originalTitle: What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash
summary: More than 500 passengers were on board the trains when the incident occurred in the province of Toledo, south of Madrid.
content:
Watch: Aerial footage shows train crash scene

Two trains have collided in Spain just south of the capital Madrid on Wednesday morning.

Rail operator Adif says the incident occurred between a Renfe train and another of the Iryo company, which covers the Madrid to Seville route.

So far at least 68 people are confirmed to have died in the incident.

Here is what we know about the crash so far.

Where and when did the crash happen?

The two trains collided just after 09:00 (08:00 GMT) between municipalities Mora and Orgaz, and about 140km (100 miles) south of Madrid.

The accident happened when a high-speed train travelling from Madrid to the south of the country collided with another train that was apparently stationary. The crash caused at least two carriages to fall down an embankment.

Broadcaster RTVE, quoting the transport ministry, said a Renfe train rear-ended an Iryo train.

Renfe is Spain's national state-owned railway company while Iryo is a private high-speed railway operator.

All train traffic on this line has been stopped at stations along the route, Adif said.

Renfe said services between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia remain suspended.

A passenger on board one of the trains told local media there was a heavy impact about 40 minutes into the journey.

Iryo said its train was "struck from behind" by a Renfe train "due to causes that are still unknown.

Transport minister Oscar Puente has said a computer failure led to the initial halt of six moving trains, including the two trains that subsequently collided.

"In the event of a system failure, the control centre takes over," he said, adding it was the control centre which decided to allow the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions.

That decision, Puente said, was made "under inexplicable circumstances". It resulted in the Renfe train crashing into the Iryo train, which was stationary on the tracks further ahead.

Bloodied, dazed and angry - how passengers' rail journey turned to disaster in Spain

High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain

Aerial footage shows the extent of the damage and the emergency response

More than 500 people were believed to be on board both trains.

Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the government of Castilla-La Mancha region, told TVE that one of the trains - managed by the Iryo company - was carrying 146 passengers plus one baby, while the Renfe-managed train had 397 passengers on board.

A former government minister was also among those reported missing.

The Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations (CEOE) posted on X that, Fátima Báñez - who heads the organization's foundation - was on board one of the trains involved in the crash.

The Castilla La Mancha regional government said 64 people are now confirmed to have died.

Speaking separately to Spanish media, he warned the death toll could increase further.

Eighty people are being treated for injuries, according to authorities, with 50 of the casualties said to be in a serious condition , and 15 more in a critical condition.

How have the authorities responded?

A huge emergency response is underway

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said "the whole of Spain is grieving" and that "lives have been shattered, families have been torn apart".

"The pain is immense," he said on a visit to the crash site.

The government was "trying to determine what was the origin of this tragedy, of this terrible accident," he added.

"We will get to the bottom of this, and if there has been any negligence, it will come to light.

"If there have been failures in the security system, they will be addressed with the utmost firmness."

Sánchez and other Spanish politicians have cancelled all public engagements on Wednesday, including campaigning for next month's parliamentary elections.

Spain's royal family posted on X that it was "shocked and concerned" and expressed condolences for the relatives of the deceased and those affected by the crash.

A spokesperson for the EU said the bloc was ready to help Spain if needed.

A huge emergency response was under way with fire crews and helicopters at the scene.

Hospitals in the area have suspended planned surgeries as they deal with an influx of patients from the crash, Spanish media have reported.

A blood transfusion centre in Madrid has also appealed for "urgent" donations. In a post on X, Centro de Transfusión said it made the request "in the face of a possible sudden increase in care needs".

It reported that facilities in Toledo, Ciudad Real and Alcázar de San Juan have cancelled procedures as casualties from the crash begin to arrive.

This is the second high-speed rail tragedy in Spain this year.

In January a high-speed train derailed in southern Spain , its rear carriages going into the path of a state-run Renfe train, claiming the lives of 46 people.

chineseTitle: 到目前为止我们对西班牙致命火车事故的了解
chineseSummary: 事件发生在马德里南部托莱多省，火车上有 500 多名乘客。
chineseContent:
观看：航拍镜头显示火车相撞现场

周三早上，西班牙首都马德里以南的两列火车相撞。

铁路运营商阿迪夫表示，这起事件发生在西班牙国家铁路公司 (Renfe) 的一列火车和 Iryo 公司的另一列火车之间，该公司覆盖马德里至塞维利亚的路线。

截至目前，已确认至少68人在该事件中死亡。

以下是迄今为止我们对此次事故的了解。

事故发生在何时何地？

两列火车于 09:00（格林威治标准时间 08:00）刚过，在马德里以南约 140 公里（100 英里）处的莫拉市和奥尔加斯市之间相撞。

事故发生时，一列从马德里开往该国南部的高速列车与另一列显然静止的列车相撞。事故导致至少两辆马车坠落路堤。

RTVE广播公司援引交通运输部的话称，一辆Renfe列车追尾了一辆Iryo列车。

Renfe 是西班牙国家国有铁路公司，Iryo 是一家私营高速铁路运营商。

阿迪夫说，该线路上的所有火车交通均已在沿线车站停止。

Renfe表示，马德里、雷阿尔城和安达卢西亚之间的服务仍然暂停。

其中一列火车上的一名乘客告诉当地媒体，行程大约 40 分钟后发生了严重撞击。

Iryo表示，其列车被Renfe列车“从后面撞上”，“原因尚不清楚”。

交通部长奥斯卡·普恩特表示，计算机故障导致六列行驶中的火车最初停止运行，其中包括随后相撞的两列火车。

他说：“如果系统出现故障，控制中心就会接管。”他补充说，是控制中心决定允许列车再次行驶，且不限速。

普恩特说，这一决定是“在无法解释的情况下”做出的。结果，Renfe 列车撞上了停在前方铁轨上的 Iryo 列车。

血迹斑斑、茫然又愤怒——西班牙乘客的铁路旅程如何变成灾难

西班牙高速列车相撞事故造成至少68人死亡

航拍镜头显示了受损程度和应急响应

据信两列火车上都有超过 500 人。

卡斯蒂利亚-拉曼恰地区政府发言人 Esther Padilla 告诉 TVE，其中一列由 Iryo 公司管理的火车载有 146 名乘客和一名婴儿，而 Renfe 管理的火车上载有 397 名乘客。

据报道失踪者中还包括一名前政府部长。

西班牙商业组织联合会 (CEOE) 在 X 上发布消息称，该组织基金会负责人法蒂玛·巴涅斯 (Fátima Báñez) 就在参与事故的一列火车上。

卡斯蒂利亚拉曼恰地区政府表示，目前已确认有 64 人死亡。

他单独向西班牙媒体发表讲话，警告死亡人数可能会进一步增加。

据当局称，80 人正在接受治疗，其中 50 人伤势严重，另有 15 人情况危急。

当局如何回应？

大规模紧急响应正在进行中

西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯表示，“整个西班牙都在悲伤”，“生活支离破碎，家庭支离破碎”。

“痛苦是巨大的，”他在参观坠机现场时说道。

他补充说，政府正在“试图确定这场悲剧、这场可怕事故的根源是什么”。

“我们会追查到底，如果有任何疏忽，就会被揭露。

“如果安全系统出现故障，我们将坚决予以解决。”

桑切斯和其他西班牙政界人士取消了周三的所有公共活动，包括为下个月的议会选举进行竞选活动。

西班牙王室在X上发帖表示“感到震惊和担忧”，并向死者亲属和受空难影响的人们表示哀悼。

欧盟发言人表示，如有需要，欧盟已准备好帮助西班牙。

消防人员和直升机正在现场进行大规模紧急响应。

据西班牙媒体报道，该地区的医院因坠机事故导致大量患者涌入，已暂停计划中的手术。

马德里的一家输血中心也呼吁“紧急”捐款。 Centro de Transfusión 在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，它是“面对护理需求可能突然增加的情况”提出这一请求的。

据报道，随着坠机事故中的伤亡人员陆续抵达，托莱多、雷阿尔城和圣胡安堡的设施已经取消了相关程序。

这是西班牙今年第二起高铁惨案。

1月份，一列高速列车在西班牙南部脱轨，后车厢冲入国营Renfe列车的轨道，造成46人死亡。
